profile_text.body:
Anthropic is a for-profit startup founded in 2021 and headquartered in San Francisco, California. Its site presents Claude as its AI, described as built for problem solvers and aimed at complex challenges, data analysis, code writing, and hard thinking work. The company's tracked products are Claude, a general LLM assistant; the Anthropic Console, an API management console with prompt testing, evaluation tools, usage monitoring, and cost controls; Claude Code, described as agentic coding with source-code exposure; and Computer Use (Anthropic), a computer control agent for desktop automation that carries system access and high-privilege operation risk.

Anthropic's legal record is substantial. Twelve cases are listed, spanning the Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit and district courts in the Northern District of California, Delaware, Hawaii, Vermont, and the Eastern District of Pennsylvania. Named matters include Edelson, PC, et al. v. Anthropic, PBC; University of Tennessee Research Foundation v. Anthropic PBC; Brunell v. Anthropic PBC; Gribble v. Anthropic PBC; Haugland v. Anthropic PBC in both Delaware and Hawaii; Patel v. Anthropic, PBC; Smith v. Anthropic, PBC; Pascual v. Anthropic, PBC; Grossinger v. Anthropic, PBC; Shakespeare v. Anthropic PBC; and Kahn v. Anthropic PBC. California is listed as a jurisdiction with a count of 264.

An MCP server is listed under the name ai.getvda/llm-orchestration-agent-langchain-anthropic, described as an LLM orchestration agent built with LangChain and Anthropic.
